messages:
Sophie (support): DataCorp reporting a bunch of 401s since midnight, response body: 'error': 'invalid_api_key'. Their app rotated keys via k8s + Vault, can we triage?
Ravi (eng): I'm on it. Any sample request/trace?
Sophie (support): pasted curl from their logs:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer s3cr3t..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
Sophie (support): They say it worked before rotation, now immediately 401.
Ravi (eng): Quick check: the token in curl is truncated in logs, can you get exact header value (raw bytes)?
Sophie (support): Got from container: `cat /etc/keys/dc_api_key` -> `s3cr3tkey\n` (note trailing newline)
Ravi (eng): Trailing newline can break some auth parsing depending on client; also if they used `X-Api-Key` header we expect either `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `Api-Key: <key>` — are they using a custom header?
Sophie (support): Their service is sending `X-API-KEY: s3cr3tkey` (uppercase). We accept `Api-Key` or `Authorization`, but the newline + subPath issue could still cause the token mismatch.
Akshay (support): Also saw similar when symlink pointed to old file after rotation — process kept an open fd to the old file. Any chance their deployment replaced symlink but didn't restart container?
Customer (DataCorp): We rotated via Vault agent, it created a new file and updated the symlink, but our pods use `subPath` in the volumeMount so the container still has the old file contents. Also our CI pipeline accidentally added a trailing CRLF.
Ravi (eng): That explains it. `subPath` copies the file into the pod at mount time and won't follow symlink updates. Two suggestions: (1) restart pods after rotation, (2) use projected volume / CSI driver that refreshes secrets, or (3) fetch the key at runtime from Vault to avoid fs symlink churn.
Sophie (support): Repro steps we asked the customer to run:
- `kubectl exec -it pod -- cat /etc/keys/dc_api_key | xxd` (inspect trailing bytes)
- `tr -d '\n' < /etc/keys/dc_api_key > /tmp/cleankey` then curl with header `Authorization: Bearer $(cat /tmp/cleankey)`
They ran this and the request stopped returning 401s.
Customer (DataCorp): Confirmed restarting pods fixed it for us. Removed the extra newline in CI and switched to a projected volume for the next deploy. Thanks!
Sophie (support): Adding a KB note about `subPath` vs symlink and trimming newlines from secret files; closing the ticket.
Ravi (eng): I'll add a short blurb to infra-runbook and flag if we see repeats.
Sophie (support): :white_check_mark:
